Equal centroid base keeps pure-base cuts fixed. For a nonvertical cap use a unit continuous coefficient and parallel translation between the two centroids. Each old fiber loses at most its maximal section volume times the displacement, uniformly over base tilt and including d=1 counting.
Every new through-centroid cap therefore has at least βm+σ−L_0R_0δ/(m+δ) mass. The proposed inequality makes this at least β(m+δ). General containing caps are no smaller.

Inside a fixed bounded source one common finite R_0 suffices for all small enlargements. Positive old slack would allow one with strictly larger mass, contradicting maximality. Existence of such balanced additions is an explicit hypothesis.
